description:
Apply the workspace extras-preservation policy (JMAP-lbdy) to crate-jmap-types.

In scope (public Deserialize structs that are wire-shaped):
- GetResponse<T>, SetResponse<T>, ChangesResponse, QueryResponse, QueryChangesResponse (methods.rs)
- AddedItem, SetError (methods.rs)
- JmapRequest, JmapResponse (wire.rs)
- Other wire-shaped structs that derive Deserialize and round-trip through HTTP

Out of scope:
- MethodResponseError (already has extras field; verify its existing pattern matches the new policy and document).
- PatchObject (already a Map<String, Value>; redundant).
- Id, UTCDate, Date, State (newtypes wrapping a single value).
- Argument<T>, ResultReference (these are recursive on T; may need recursive treatment depending on design).
- Filter<T>, FilterOperator<T>, Operator (filter algebra — DECIDED OUT 2026-05-10 per parent JMAP-lbdy "Decision: filter algebra excluded": silent-drop foot-gun at server, `#[serde(untagged)]` dispatch incompatible with extras pattern, control enum must dispatch on known variants. `#[non_exhaustive]` already gives spec-level forward-compat).
- Invocation (tuple type — cannot add a struct field).

Cookie-cutter consistency: jmap-types is the foundation type crate per workspace AGENTS.md; scope and field-shape are inherited from parent epic JMAP-lbdy and apply identically across the workspace. Each migrated struct adds one field with the documented attribute; no public types added/renamed/removed.

Acceptance: every in-scope struct has `pub extra: Map<String, Value>` with the documented attributes; one round-trip preservation test per type; PLAN.md updated; cargo test/clippy/fmt clean.
title: Adopt extras policy in jmap-types
